fixes.explanation: Right on, baker. David says this person "…does no harm to his neighbor…" (Psalm 15:3). Easy to be nice to strangers you'll never see again. Your neighbor is the one who sees your trash cans every week.
It's actually true. Psalm 15:3 says he "…does no harm to his neighbor…" That's a person he's around and could easily wrong. I think that's why this one lands so hard.

Nope, money isn't what this verse names. David says he "…honors those who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 15:4). Great wealth isn't the group the psalm points to here. The honor goes to those who fear the LORD.
Not quite, friend. The verse says he "…honors those who fear the LORD…" (Psalm 15:4). Armies don't show up in this psalm. The group David names is those who fear the LORD.

Right. The psalm says he "…does not revise a costly oath…" (Psalm 15:4). Costly means keeping it hurts, and he keeps it anyway. It's like a baker who promised a dozen boxes, found out it'd take all night, and kept the oven on.

Close, but listen to the exact words. David says he "…lends his money without interest…" (Psalm 15:5). Interest is the thing the psalm says he leaves off. A small fee isn't what this verse talks about.

Ha, I get it, that's how a lot of us start. But the psalm says he "…refuses a bribe against the innocent." (Psalm 15:5). The verse tells us where he lands, and it's a flat no. Whatever the envelope holds, the answer is refuse.
